The Xperience is an immersive art and theme park on the hillside of Lipa Noi, on Koh Samui's west coast, that opened in early 2026. It has 12 themed zones with more than 100 artworks: giant sculptures, a heart-shaped lagoon with a beach club, infinity pools, light mazes, and projection mapping and fire shows after dark. It is open Wednesday to Sunday from 11:00 to 22:00, and until midnight on Fridays. A Day Pass costs 1,500 THB per person, and children aged 0–2 go free. Thursdays, Saturdays and Sundays are Family Days; Wednesdays and Fridays are for over-16s only.

Opening days, hours and who can go

The park keeps a five-day week and changes character by the day. The age rule is the thing that catches visitors out: on Wednesday and Friday nobody under 16 is allowed in, so families need to pick a Thursday, Saturday or Sunday.

Open now? [kp_open spec="We,Th,Sa,Su 11:00-22:00; Fr 11:00-24:00"]

The park was designed for adults, so even on Family Days children must stay with a parent the whole time. Babies and toddlers aged 0–2 enter free; from age 3, children pay the full Day Pass price.

Tickets and prices

The Day Pass is the ticket most visitors need. It covers the whole public park for the day, from opening until closing, including the pools, every art zone, the evening light show and the fire show. Tickets are limited each day, and walk-ins are not guaranteed, so book before you travel to the west coast.

Good to know: we sell the Day Pass at the park's own price of 1,500 THB, paid securely by card in Thai baht. Choose your date, and we book your entry in your name for that day and send your confirmation by email. Food, drinks, VIP areas, wellness treatments and transport are paid separately.

What's inside: the 12 zones

The park climbs a jungle hillside, so most visitors take one of the park's golf carts to the top and walk back down through the zones. Allow at least three hours just to see everything once.

ZoneWhat you'll findBest time
The PlayaThe beach club: white sand, day beds and hammocks around what the park bills as the world's largest heart-shaped lagoon, with giant white sculptures watching over the waterAfternoon swim, sunset
AfrikaBurnTall metal spires inspired by the AfrikaBurn festival that breathe fire after dark; the park calls it "welcome to Mars"After dark
LunaA valley of lights around DJ Luna, a giant figure who comes alive with projection mapping at nightAfter dark
Sky BarThe highest point of the park, with an infinity pool hanging over the hillside and views over the west coastSunset
Mystic VillageThe wellness village: a projection-mapped 360° dome, flotation, ice baths, sauna, sound healing and yoga, plus the Mystic CaféAny time
Art HouseA forest of mirror-polished stainless-steel sculptures that reflect the jungle around themDaylight
The WoodsAn enchanted woodland trail with a quiet zen cornerDaylight
MyceliumA nature zone built around the idea of the underground fungus networkDaylight and dusk
Alien JungleDozens of huge metal creatures inspired by Alien vs. Predator, hidden in the treesDaylight
Labyrinth LightsA maze with 30 interactive light installationsAfter dark
Recycled ArtThirty spaces for artists working with recycled materials, including creatures made from old tyresDaylight
Hippie CampA colourful camp of painted vans, music and festival décorLate afternoon and evening

Look out for the pink sandstone village with its fairy-tale towers and giant stone hands, the frog-shaped golf carts, and costumed performers who wander the park on busy days. Many of the statues are hyper-realistic figures that the park says are the first of their kind, and photos are encouraged everywhere.

Day and night: two different parks

Visitors who stay for the evening say the park feels like a different place once the sun goes down. By day it's a sculpture garden with pools and a lagoon; after sunset, the trees, spires and statues light up in neon, the giant figures come alive with projection mapping, and the fire performers start. On the west coast the sun sets over the sea at about 17:55 in November and about 18:45 in July, so the light show starts earlier in the cool season.

Fridays are the big night. The Xperience After Dark keeps the park open until midnight with live DJs, illuminated landscapes, fire performances and sunset cocktails across 12 art zones and 3 pools. It is 16+ only, and the Day Pass covers it.

Food, drinks and wellness

Outside food and drink are not allowed, so plan to eat in the park. The kitchen works farm to table, from wild edible ferns to freshly caught fish.

OutletWhat it servesWhen
The Playa Beach ClubGlobal dishes and cocktails by the lagoonDuring park hours
Mystic CaféFresh juices and signature drinks in Mystic VillageDuring park hours
Sky BarDrinks with a view from the top of the park; sunset dining announced by the parkCheck on the day
Luna BarCocktails and lounge service by the Luna light showFridays
Dining "At Playa"Private chef's dinner by the lagoon, from 15,000 THB per person, wine pairing 10,000 THB extra; first 12 guests only, weather permitting17:30–21:00, by booking

Early reviews describe the food as good but drink prices as high for Samui; budget roughly what you would pay at a west-coast beach club. Residents with the 500 THB pass get 20% off food and drink. In Mystic Village you can book wellness sessions: the projection dome, flotation pods, ice baths, sauna, sound healing and yoga. The park does not publish wellness prices online, so ask at the village when you arrive.

How to plan your visit

Most visitors who loved it arrived in the afternoon and stayed until the night show. This is the plan we suggest for a first visit:

  1. 14:30 Leave your hotel; allow 40–50 minutes from Chaweng or Bophut, 30–40 from Lamai.
  2. 15:15 Arrive, show your booking and take a golf cart to the top of the park.
  3. 15:30 Walk down through Sky Bar, Art House, Alien Jungle and The Woods while it's light.
  4. 16:30 Swim and relax at The Playa lagoon; order an early dinner at the beach club.
  5. 17:55 Sunset (November; later in summer), then watch the park light up.
  6. 18:30 Labyrinth Lights, Luna and the projection mapping; fire show at AfrikaBurn.
  7. 21:30 Head back to your driver (on Fridays you can stay until midnight).

What to bring and the house rules

  • Swimwear and sunscreen for the pools and the lagoon
  • Comfortable shoes: paths run up and down a jungle hillside
  • Mosquito repellent for the evening
  • A hat and water for the afternoon
  • Your booking confirmation and, for residents, proof of residence
  • A costume if you want to join in (or try for a free Costume Pass)
  • No outside food or drink
  • No pets
  • No drugs, no nudity
  • Don't climb on or damage the art: visitors are liable for damage
  • You may be filmed or photographed for the park's marketing

Is it worth 1,500 THB?

For most people, yes, if you give it the afternoon and evening. Nothing else on Koh Samui looks like it: the scale of the sculptures, the lagoon and the night show are a genuine full-day outing, and early visitor reviews are overwhelmingly positive. The common complaints are the price (1,500 THB is more than most Samui attractions) and drinks prices, and some visitors found it quiet on weekdays, which others saw as a plus.

Good for: couples, groups of friends, photographers and content creators, families with older children on a Family Day, a rainy-season afternoon when the sea is rough, and anyone staying on the west or south coast.

Go elsewhere if:

  • You only have an hour or two. You'll pay the full Day Pass and miss the night show, which is the highlight.
  • You want a cheap beach day. A free beach and a sunset drink at a Lipa Noi beach bar costs a fraction; see Koh Samui sunset spots.
  • You want a late party every night. Apart from Friday, the park closes at 22:00; for clubs after midnight see Chaweng nightlife.
  • You have small children and can only go on a Wednesday or Friday. Try Koh Samui with kids for other ideas.

Getting there

The Xperience is in the hills above Lipa Noi, about 5 minutes by car from Nikki Beach and 10–15 minutes south of Nathon. Grab works in the daytime, but drivers are scarce on the west coast after dark, and taxis rarely wait, so plan your ride home before you go.

The easiest way to do the afternoon-and-night plan is a private van with driver: 8 hours costs 4,500 THB for up to 10 people, and the driver waits and takes you home after the show. More on getting around Koh Samui; don't ride a scooter back after drinks on the dark hill roads.

Weather on the day

Most of the park is outdoors, and there is shade, cafés and covered spaces to wait out a shower. In the wet season (October to December) showers often pass quickly, but November can bring days of steady rain, so check the forecast below. Make a weekend of it

The Xperience pairs well with a morning on the water. Our Pig Island speedboat tour (1,450 THB adult, 1,250 THB child) runs all year and is back by early afternoon. The Ang Thong speedboat tour (1,800 THB adult, 1,400 THB child) restarts on 16 December 2026, when the park reopens after its 1 November–15 December closure. For the evening after, a private yacht sunset cruise is on Koh Samui boat charter.
